question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3})\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+{x}^{3}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the chain and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3})\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+{x}^{3}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)) & =(3{x}^{2})\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+{x}^{3}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(xy) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-{x}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\cdot y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-{x}^{3}y\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\cdot (1) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-{x}^{3}y\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$
